transcript.text: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The OE code on your LG washing machine means it has detected that water hasn't drained within about 13 minutes. This is almost always caused by a blockage in the drain pump filter or the drain hose, rather than a broken part. We need to be very careful. Opening the main filter directly with water inside will release a lot of water. 1. Check for external blockages first: Ensure the drain hose at the back isn't kinked or crushed against the wall, and that it isn't pushed too far down into your sink waste or standpipe (it should only go in about 15cm).
2. Tilt to inspect: If you have help, tilt the machine back slightly on its front edge (put a towel underneath) so you can look under the bottom right corner. You might see if the drain hose is kinked or if there's any obvious obstruction.
3. Safe filter access: If you can safely open the small kickplate at the bottom right without water gushing out, do so. Inside, you'll see a small tube (emergency drain) and the main filter cap. Do not unscrew the main filter yet. Check if the emergency drain tube is blocked or if you can see debris in the opening. Please let me know what you find with these checks. If you are unable to tilt it or access the bottom safely, tell me that, and we will try a different approach.

I checked the hose - the machine was pushed right back against the wall and the hose was squashed behind it, so I've pulled it out and straightened it. Still not touching that filter though, and I'm not tilting it on my laminate floor.

Since straightening the hose hasn't cleared the OE code, the blockage is likely inside the machine at the filter or in the pump itself. 1. Switch the machine off and unplug it for safety.
2. Plug it back in and start a 'Drain' or 'Spin' programme.
3. Listen carefully near the bottom right corner where the filter is. Does the pump make a humming, buzzing, or grinding noise (trying to push water), or is there total silence? This tells us if the motor is working but blocked, or if it has failed completely.
I ran the spin again after straightening the hose. It drained a little slower than normal, then OE came up again. The pump does hum, and I've heard an occasional rattle too.

The humming sound with occasional rattling suggests that the pump motor is working but something is physically blocking the impeller (the fan inside) or the filter is heavily clogged. The rattle could be a coin, button, or hairpin spinning around. We cannot just unscrew the main filter yet—that will release all that water at once. We need to drain it out slowly first using the emergency tube if one is present. Is there a small, thin tube sticking out near the larger circular filter cap? If so, tell me exactly what you see. If there isn't one, we will have to use towels and a shallow tray to catch the water from the main filter, but let's check for that tube first.

I haven't opened the cover so I can't tell you what's in there. I'm not unscrewing the main filter, towels and tray or not. If there's a small tube, what exactly would I be opening, and how do I stop it flooding my laminate again?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. I understand your concern about flooding. The small tube you see is called the emergency drain hose (usually a thin, flexible grey or black tube with a cap). It is designed specifically to let water out slowly so you don't have to open the main filter cap while there is still water inside. Here is exactly how to use it safely on your laminate floor:
1. Place a shallow tray, a large baking tin, or several thick towels directly in front of that small tube.
2. Pull the tube out slightly (it might be tucked behind the flap). Remove its cap and let the water drain into your tray/towels. Once most of the water is gone, put the cap back on tightly.
3. Only then should you unscrew the large circular main filter cap slowly. Because you have drained most of the water via the tube, only a small amount will spill out when you open the main filter. This prevents the flood you experienced last time. Once the main filter is out, check for coins, buttons, or hairpins caught in the plastic impeller behind it. Clean it and reassemble. If you are not comfortable doing this step yourself, given your previous bad experience with flooding, I would recommend calling a local engineer to clear the blockage safely.

Ok, I'll do the small tube only, with the towels and baking tray down. But I'm still not unscrewing the main filter, my husband can do that at the weekend. Do I just take the cap off the tube and let it run out?

Yes, just take the cap off and let it run into your tray or towels. It will likely only give you a cup or two of water—that's all the emergency tube can hold—but it reduces the pressure so that when your husband eventually opens the main filter, it won't flood. Please wait until the dripping has completely stopped before doing anything else. Once it is empty, let me know and we can look at what to do next.
Ok, I'll do that now with the towels and tray down. Will let you know once it's stopped dripping.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That sounds like a sensible plan. Just let me know once that small tube has finished dripping into your tray and towels. There is probably something blocking the impeller inside—likely a coin, button, or hairpin caught in the filter area. Draining via the emergency tube removes the pressure so it won't flood when that blockage is finally cleared. If your husband is happy to do it at the weekend, he will simply need to place towels under the flap, unscrew the main cap slowly (any remaining water will drip out), remove any debris from the filter and the hole behind it, check the plastic impeller spins freely by hand, then screw it back on tight. If you'd rather not have him touch it at all, or if he finds nothing wrong with the filter once it's open, we can discuss calling an engineer to clear it safely. Just let me know when the dripping stops and what your preference is.
Ok, it's stopped dripping now. I've put the cap back on. Husband will do the main filter at the weekend. Anything else I should do until then?

That sounds like a solid plan. Until your husband gets to it this weekend, there is nothing else you need to do—just leave the machine switched off and unplugged. If it clears that code and spins normally, you are good to go.
